question: In which Article of the Indian Constitution it is mentioned that 'the advice tendered by the Ministers to the Governor shall not be inquired into by any Court'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 163**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 163** of the Indian Constitution states that the Governor of a state is aided and advised by the Council of Ministers in exercising his functions, except where he is required to act in his discretion.
 
• This article explicitly mentions that **"the advice tendered by the Ministers to the Governor shall not be inquired into by any Court."**
 
• The provision ensures the confidentiality of the advice given by the Council of Ministers to the Governor, preserving the sanctity of the constitutional process.
 
• This article is crucial for maintaining the **separation of powers** and ensuring that the executive's internal workings remain immune from judicial scrutiny.
 
• The Governor's discretion is limited to specific areas as mentioned in the Constitution, and in most other matters, he is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• This provision upholds the principle of responsible governance under the parliamentary system, where the Council of Ministers holds collective responsibility.
 
• By shielding the advice tendered from judicial review, **Article 163** safeguards the democratic functioning of state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 167**__
 __
 
• **Article 167** of the Indian Constitution lays down the duties of the Chief Minister in relation to the Governor.
 
• It states that the Chief Minister shall communicate all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor and furnish any information related to the administration of the state.
 
• The Chief Minister may also submit proposals for consideration by the Council of Ministers if required by the Governor.
 
• This provision ensures a smooth flow of information and coordination between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Article 161**__
 __
 
• **Article 161** gives the Governor the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit, or commute sentences in cases relating to offenses against laws in the state.
 
• This is similar to the President's power under **Article 72**, but is limited to state laws.
 
• This article highlights the Governor's role in the criminal justice system of the state.
 
 
 
• **Article 168**__
 
 
• **Article 168** establishes the structure of the state legislature, which consists of the Governor and either one or two houses depending on the state.
 
• In states with a bicameral legislature, the two houses are called the **Legislative Assembly** and the **Legislative Council**.
 
• This article highlights the legislative framework of state governments in India.
